title: 投资经典：Buffett 核心原则 — Day 1
title_en: Investing Classics: Buffett's Core Principles — Day 1

questions.question: 按 Buffett 对「能力圈」的论述，对投资者最重要的是什么？
options: 只要长期持有、跟踪过某个行业，就可以算作在圈内
清楚知道圈子的边界并只在圈内下注，圈子的大小并不重要
圈子一经确定就固定不变，圈外领域应一概拒绝学习
不断扩大圈子，覆盖尽可能多的行业和公司，以免错过任何好机会
questions.explanation: Buffett 1996 年信中说，圈子大小不重要，知道边界才至关重要；边界感是一道防御工事。把「持有过」当成「懂」是常见误用；能力圈也可以靠深度学习扩展（如用熟悉的消费品牌框架理解 Apple），用「圈外」为拒绝学习开脱同样不对。
questions.question_en: According to Buffett's idea of the 'circle of competence,' what matters most for an investor?
options_en: Any industry you've held or followed for a long time counts as being inside your circle
Knowing exactly where the circle's boundary lies and betting only inside it; the circle's size matters little
Once set, the circle never changes, and areas outside it should never be studied
Constantly widening the circle to cover as many industries as possible so no opportunity is missed
questions.explanation_en: In his 1996 letter Buffett said the size of the circle is not very important but knowing its boundaries is vital; that sense of boundary is a defense. Mistaking 'I've owned it' for 'I understand it' is a common misuse. The circle can be widened through deep study (e.g., understanding Apple through a familiar consumer-brand lens), so using 'outside my circle' as an excuse not to learn is also wrong.

questions.question: 评估一家公司有没有真正的护城河，最核心的问题是什么？
options: 它目前的市场占有率是否在行业里排名第一
它当前的利润率是否处在自身历史的最高位
它最近几年的收入增速是否明显快于同行
对手为什么拿不走它的高回报，十年后它是否还能赚这么多
questions.explanation: 护城河回答的是「为什么对手不能轻易拿走你的利润」，看重的是回报的持久性：ROIC 25% 但年年被蚕食的公司，长期价值不如 ROIC 18% 但稳如磐石的公司。高市占率是结果不是原因，无壁垒的高增长最危险。
questions.question_en: When judging whether a company has a real moat, what is the central question?
options_en: Is its current market share the largest in the industry?
Is its current profit margin at the highest level in its own history?
Has its revenue grown noticeably faster than its peers in recent years?
Why can't competitors take away its high returns, and will it still earn this much ten years from now?
questions.explanation_en: A moat answers why rivals can't easily take your profits, and what counts is durability: a 25% ROIC eroding two points a year is worth less long-term than a rock-steady 18%. High market share is an outcome, not a cause, and fast growth without barriers is the most dangerous kind.

questions.question: 你持有的一只股票一个月内跌了 30%。按 Graham 和 Buffett 的「市场先生」思路，下一步该怎么想？
options: 价格下跌说明市场掌握了你不知道的信息，应先止损再说
波动率就是风险，应先减仓、降低组合的 Beta 再观察
价格大跌本身就是市场先生递来的礼物，应坚持按原计划逢跌加仓、越跌越买
先对照自己事先独立估出的内在价值区间，判断下跌是基本面变化还是情绪
questions.explanation: 市场先生的报价是选项不是义务，但利用他的前提是你已独立估算了内在价值；没有价值锚的人只会被他玩弄。「逢跌就买」是误用，基本面恶化时市场先生有时是对的（价值陷阱）。Buffett 恰恰反对用波动率衡量风险。
questions.question_en: A stock you own falls 30% in a month. Following Graham and Buffett's 'Mr. Market' idea, how should you think about the next step?
options_en: A falling price means the market knows something you don't, so cut the loss first and think later
Volatility is risk, so trim the position and lower the portfolio's beta before watching further
A big price drop is itself a gift from the market, so stick to the plan and buy more the further it falls
Check it against the intrinsic-value range you estimated independently beforehand, and judge whether the drop reflects fundamentals or mood
questions.explanation_en: Mr. Market's quotes are options, not obligations, but exploiting them presupposes that you've independently estimated intrinsic value; without that anchor he plays you instead. 'Buy every dip' is a misuse, since Mr. Market is sometimes right when fundamentals deteriorate (a value trap). Buffett explicitly rejects volatility as the measure of risk.
